SMTO-PRX-0010 — Proxmox task failed

GUID: e5c3797d-947a-4fea-a62c-4294c0ecbc3f
Slug: proxmox-task-failed
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • SMTO asked Proxmox to do the job, and Proxmox itself reported that the job ended with an error. The VM may still be in its earlier state, or it may be partly changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Proxmox web interface, select the VM, and open its Task History to read the error for this task. Proxmox records the exact reason the job failed, such as a locked VM or not enough memory.
  2. Fix the cause Proxmox reports, for example wait for another task on the VM to finish, or free up memory or storage on that node. Asking again without fixing the cause will fail the same way.
  3. Ask the Agent to show the VM's current status, and ask for the action again only if it's still needed. A failed job can still leave some changes behind, so checking first avoids doing the work twice.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reports the VM in the state you asked for, and Proxmox's Task History shows the new task ended with OK.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, together with the error from Proxmox's Task History, to the person who manages the Proxmox server. Don't remove locks or loosen security settings on Proxmox just to make the task pass.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Proxmox task failed.

What this means

  • Task polling observes status stopped with exitstatus other than OK. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • Task polling observes status stopped with exitstatus other than OK.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact UPID and task log; failed completion does not imply that every intermediate change rolled back.

How to fix it

  • The task's UPID and exitstatus are in the error facts. Read that task's log in the Proxmox GUI (the VM's or node's Task History) or through the node's tasks API, fix the recorded cause (for example a lock, missing storage or insufficient resources), and read current guest state before issuing another power request.
  • Inspect the Proxmox task result and log to correct its recorded cause.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The task's recorded failure and resulting guest state are understood before additional changes.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
